newsitem.title: USA: China MFN should be delinked from campaign finance.
newsitem.headline: China MFN should be delinked from campaign finance.

text.p: Extending Most-Favored Nation trading status to China should not be linked to the outcome of continuing campaign finance investigations, House Banking Chairman James Leach said in a speech Tuesday.

"The issues: MFN, which is fundamentally about relations between two peoples, and campaign finance abuses, which are about the foolish actions of a few, are distinct," Leach told the Hong Kong Trade Development Council.

"...it is crucial that the issue of extending normal non- discriminatory trading benefits to China should be delinked from aberrations", in this case campaign finance investigations, he said in his speech.

China's trade status is reviewed annually by lawmakers. President Bill Clinton has until June to decide on MFN, which allows Chinese goods into the country at the same low tariff rates as goods from almost all other countries.

"Congress should not hesitate to rewew China's MFN status, preferably on a multi-year basis with less counter-productive conditionality," Leach told the group. Congress has to decide whether or not to overturn Clinton's decision. This year, Congress will be taking a hard look at how China deals with Hong Kong after it takes control on July 1.
